policy_note: Dutch writes an apostrophe inside ordinary words -- 's morgens, auto's -- so it must never be rejected, and the token pattern keeps it inside a token. Hyphenated compounds (zee-eend) are likewise ordinary. nl-v2 adds the reduced words that BEGIN with an apostrophe ('t, 'n, 's, 'm, 'k) to the scoring tokenizer, so a sentence containing 't is scored as containing a rank-58 word rather than a bare 't'. The list is closed on purpose: an open leading apostrophe would read a quoted 'hallo as a different word from hallo. Matching cards is unaffected by this pattern; apostrophe surfaces are found by the matcher's literal path.
